package.name: @google/gemini-cli
package.installedWith: npm install --ignore-scripts --save-exact, into a throwaway folder

why: LIMIT 1: Gemini expands $VAR in its settings from its own process environment at start-up, so the pass must be in that environment, and a command in its shell can read it from there (ps eww on macOS; /proc/<pid>/environ on Linux, reasoned and not run). Every environment-level lever, the start-up-file workaround included, leaves it there.
LIMIT 2: the CLI has no per-variable exclusion: sanitizeEnvironment returns the whole environment unless the global redaction is enabled.

LIMIT 3: with the global redaction enabled the allow list cannot protect the person's own variables: secret-named ones (SSH_AUTH_SOCK, *_KEY, *_TOKEN) are dropped from it, and values shaped like credentials are removed before it is consulted.

geminiOwnMacOsSandboxAttempt.tried: gemini -s with GEMINI_SANDBOX=sandbox-exec and the built-in permissive-open profile, on the app's isolated-home layout
geminiOwnMacOsSandboxAttempt.firstStderrLine: Error in <throwaway>/h/.gemini/trustedFolders.json: EPERM: operation not permitted, open '<throwaway>/h/.gemini/trustedFolders.json'
geminiOwnMacOsSandboxAttempt.conclusion: it did not start with this layout (the profile does not let the CLI read the trust file kept outside its allowed folders); not pursued: it would also change what the agent may do

systemSettingsControl: Security Warning: Skipping system settings file '<throwaway>/old-system-settings.json': Parent directory '<throwaway>' is insecure: Directory '<throwaway>' is not owned by root

stands_in_for.model: scripted Gemini-API stand-in on loopback (no Google account, no key, no Gemini model)

not_tested: a real Gemini model choosing tools well
a real Gemini login, and whether the app's links carry it into an agent's home
Gemini CLI on Windows and Linux (the /proc/<pid>/environ route that LIMIT 1 predicts there is reasoned from the same design, not run)
a Gemini sandbox profile that refuses process inspection (the built-in one did not start on the app's isolated-home layout)

MEASURED: the pass IS visible to Gemini's shell, and the support matrix says "no"
the person's own variables are untouched: the app changed nothing about Gemini's shell
the provider's tokens are in no file Gemini or the app wrote
the pass is in no file Gemini or the app wrote (it is in the environment only)
neither the pass nor a provider token appears in any process argument while Gemini ran
nothing sent to the model, nor Gemini's own output, carries the pass or a provider token
the CLI's own redaction, switched on, hides the pass, and also SSH_AUTH_SOCK and every secret-looking variable (why the app does not switch it on for you)
all four scans ran inside the real Gemini shell
control (the original exposure): with the app's default settings the pass is in the environment of Gemini's shell
control: every variable a person really has reaches the shell, including SSH_AUTH_SOCK and the secret-looking ones, and BASH_ENV reaches it too (Gemini does not strip it from the shell)
LIMIT 1: the pass can be read from OUTSIDE the shell's own environment: a command in Gemini's shell reads the environment of the processes above it (ps), and it is the real pass (hash equal)
results.detail: 2 process(es) in the shell's ancestry hold it; hashes equal

results.name: LIMIT 2: the CLI has no per-variable lever: with its redaction off, naming the pass as blocked hides nothing
the global lever (redaction on, every other name allowed) does remove the pass from the shell's own environment, and keeps a plain variable

LIMIT 3: but it also hides variables that are not the pass, whatever the allow list says: SSH_AUTH_SOCK and other secret-named variables (this version drops such names from the allow list), and values shaped like credentials
results.detail: hidden although allowed by name: F9_PROBE_GH_SHAPED, ARTIFACT_MIRROR, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, MY_OWN_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY

results.name: LIMIT 1 again, with the lever on: the pass is gone from the shell's environment and is STILL readable from the processes above it (so no Gemini setting makes it inaccessible)
results.detail: 2 process(es) in the ancestry hold it

results.name: the shell start-up-file workaround (BASH_ENV unsets the pass) hides it from `env` and from nothing else: the processes above the shell still hold the real pass, so it would be a misleading fix and is not shipped
the lifecycle hooks the app wrote are loaded AND RUN by the real CLI: their payloads reached the hive socket
results.detail: 32 payloads: SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop
